fixes.explanation: True, friend. The text says Zedekiah "…did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done." (2 Kings 24:19) Jehoiakim was an earlier king of Judah, and the writer sets the two kings side by side. I think that's a heavy thing to read.

Wall is right! The army "…encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it." (2 Kings 25:1) All around, friend. That means the wall circles the whole city. It's like walking out your front door and finding a wall where your driveway used to be.

A trench is a ditch, and nobody grabs a shovel in this verse. The text says the army "…encamped outside the city and built a siege wall all around it." (2 Kings 25:1) It's a wall, not a hole in the ground. Wall is the word the text uses.

They flee by night, friend! The text says "…all the men of war fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden." (2 Kings 25:4) They headed toward the Arabah, even though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city.

They chase, friend. The text says "…the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho…" (2 Kings 25:5) The men of war left by night, but the Chaldeans went after the king and caught him. His whole army deserted him.

Letting go isn't what happens to the king. The text says "…the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho…" (2 Kings 25:5) They went after him instead of waving goodbye. Pursued means chased, and they caught him.

Extra troops aren't mentioned in this verse. The text says "…the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho…" (2 Kings 25:5) The Chaldean army is the one that pursues him.

Freedom isn't what the text gives the people who remained in the city. It says Nebuzaradan "…carried into exile the people who remained in the city…" (2 Kings 25:11) Exile means they are taken away from their land. I think it's a hard verse to read.

Nobles aren't named in this verse. The text says the captain of the guard "…left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields." (2 Kings 25:12) Poorest is the word the text uses. They're the ones left to work the land.

Singers and musicians aren't named in this verse. The text says he "…took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers." (2 Kings 25:18) So the chief priest, the second priest and the doorkeepers are the ones on the list.

Merchants and farmers aren't the ones listed. The text says he "…took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers." (2 Kings 25:18) Some of the poorest of the land were left to tend the vineyards and fields (2 Kings 25:12). The priests and doorkeepers are the ones he takes here.
